text: GPT-6 Astra 是面向 DSH Web 的编码 agent 人格预设。它把 GPT-6 / Codex Astra 指令作为 persona 配置，并通过 DSH bundle 将预设文件同步到本机预设目录，安装后可在会话的预设选择器中选用。适合希望沿用 DSH 编码工具、同时采用 Astra 风格身份与协作方式的用户。无需额外 API 密钥或外部账号。

GPT-6 Astra is a DSH Web coding-agent persona preset. It applies Astra instructions as the DSH persona and syncs preset files to the local directory for session selection. It suits users who want Astra-style guidance with DSH coding tools. No extra API key or account is needed.
想给 DSH 的编码 agent 换成更像 Codex 的协作风格。
怎么在 DSH 会话里选择 Astra 风格的人格预设？
I want a DSH coding agent to use Astra-style persona instructions.
GPT-6 Astra 的功能「编码 agent 人格」：将 Astra 指令配置为 DSH persona 的 prefix，并保留工作目录 suffix；在 DSH 会话中选择该预设即可使用。
GPT-6 Astra 的功能「自动安装预设文件」：bundle 启动时把 composition、元数据和 skills 树同步到本机预设目录，只重写内容不同的文件。

text:
dsh-preset-gpt-6-astra README · 原理：dsh 的系统提示是**按段拼装**的，`dsh-persona` 这个 row 提供两个段：

| 段 | order | 本预设内容 |
|---|---|---|
| `deployment:persona-prefix` | 0 | 两段 Astra 指令 + 运行环境适配段 |
| `deployment:persona-suffix` | 10200 | `Your working directory is {{cwd}}.` |

顺序是 **identity-first**（与 Claude Code / Codex 的惯例一致）：harness 身份段（−100）→
人格（0）→ 各工具 row 自己的指导（100–199）→ 工作目录尾段（10200）。也就是说 **dsh 的工具
指导排人格之后**，冲突时以 harness 的工具说明为准。

composition 里三条 `isolate` realm 规则（`planning` / `compaction` / `delegation`）是 dsh
对「预设自有服务」的硬要求，本仓库原样保留，未做改动。

dsh-preset-gpt-6-astra README · 成本提示：人格段常驻系统提示，约 **44 K 字符 ≈ 11k token**，每次请求都会带上。相比整份内联
（339 KB ≈ 85k token）已经是 1/8，而且：

- spawn 子代理只付 ~100 token 的人格，不再复制整份；
- 参考 skill 与原文在被读取前不产生任何 token 成本。

  `skills.list`, …) onto tools that exist here, and states which Codex product surfaces
  (Apps/Connectors, Plugins, `request_permissions`, `end_conversation`, …) do not.
- **Spawned subagents do not carry the persona** — the `tool-subagent` row (provider
  `spawn`) installs a 444-character child persona. The `subagent_fork` row deliberately
  keeps the parent persona: inheriting history and reusing the parent's KV cache is its
  whole point.

dsh-preset-gpt-6-astra README · How the persona was selected (important)：The source document is titled **“Collected prompts and templates”**: a library of prompt
fragments for **several Codex surfaces** (5,051 lines), not one system prompt. This preset
inlines only two **contiguous** blocks that are actually a coding agent's instructions:

dsh-preset-gpt-6-astra README · How the persona was selected (important)：| block | source lines | what it is |
|---|---|---|
| `## Base model instruction template` → just before `# Apps (Connectors)` | 5–157 | the model layer: identity, permission posture, autonomy, personality and writing style, working with the user, rules for getting work done, using skills |
| `## Engine default base instruction template` → end of file | 4,775–5,051 | the engine layer: the assembled Codex CLI base instruction — how you work, AGENTS.md, responsiveness, planning, task execution, validating work, ambition vs. precision, progress updates, final answer structure, tool guidelines |

dsh-preset-gpt-6-astra README · How the persona was selected (important)：The other ~4,600 lines are **deliberately excluded** because they are addressed to *other*
models: `# Classification` ends with "Output that single token immediately and nothing
else." (a classifier), plus the Guardian review templates, the approval and
`request_permissions` fragments, the browser confirmation policies, the code-review
rubric, the realtime backend, the desktop/UI fragments, and the orchestration and
compaction templates. None of it is lost — it lives in
`preset/skills/gpt-6-astra-reference/reference/` and loads on demand.

dsh-preset-gpt-6-astra README · How the persona was selected (important)：There is also a purely technical reason: line 362 contains
`{{ tenant_policy_config }}`. dsh interpolates `{{…}}` **strictly**, so an unregistered
group fails the whole turn — and `dsh-persona` has no `interpolate: false` (only sections
registered through `ctx.systemPrompt.section({ interpolate: false })` do). Inlining the
whole file would simply not mount.

dsh-preset-gpt-6-astra README · How the persona was selected (important)：To change the selection, edit `SELECTION` in `scripts/build.mjs` (start/end heading
markers) and re-run build + check; a missing anchor fails the build.

dsh-preset-gpt-6-astra README · Deliberate deviations from `standard`：`build.mjs` carries an explicit `PATCHES` list; each entry names the upstream fact it
overrides and why. If an anchor is missing (or matches more than once) in a newer
`standard`, the build **fails loudly** instead of silently dropping the change:

dsh-preset-gpt-6-astra README · Deliberate deviations from `standard`：| patch | why |
|---|---|
| `skill-filesystem` gains `customSkillDirs` (`!!js` + `baseUrl` pointing at the preset's own `skills/`) | lets the excluded text and the selection map travel with the preset and load on demand; the same mechanism the shipped `cordis` preset uses |
| `tool-subagent` (spawn) gains a 444-character `persona` | the persona is resident cost; a freshly spawned child does not need the full version. `subagent_fork` is left alone — it exists to inherit history and reuse the parent's KV cache |

dsh-preset-gpt-6-astra README · How it works：dsh assembles its system prompt from **ordered sections**; the `dsh-persona` row supplies
two of them:

| section | order | content in this preset |
|---|---|---|
| `deployment:persona-prefix` | 0 | the two Astra blocks + the run-environment adaptation |
| `deployment:persona-suffix` | 10200 | `Your working directory is {{cwd}}.` |

dsh-preset-gpt-6-astra README · How it works：Ordering is **identity-first** (the Claude Code / Codex convention): harness identity
(−100) → persona (0) → each tool row's own guidance (100–199) → the working-directory
suffix (10200). dsh's tool guidance therefore comes *after* the persona and wins on
conflict.

The three `isolate` realm rules (`planning` / `compaction` / `delegation`) are a hard
requirement dsh places on services a preset owns; they are kept exactly as upstream.

---

dsh-preset-gpt-6-astra README · Cost note：The persona section is resident: roughly **44 K characters ≈ 11k tokens** on every
request — about one eighth of inlining the whole 339 KB document. On top of that, a
spawned subagent pays ~100 tokens of persona instead of the full text, and the reference
skill costs nothing until it is loaded.

dsh-preset-gpt-6-astra README · Upgrade and maintenance (important)：dsh changes row config schemas. Gotchas this repository has hit:

- **dsh ≤ 0.1.4**: the `dsh-persona` fields were `text: <string>`.
- **Since dsh 0.1.5-rc.3**: the fields are `prefix` (required) and `suffix`; the old form
  **fails to mount** with `invalid config: $.prefix missing required value`. If that
  preset is also the default, the symptom is that **starting a new conversation fails
  outright and no session directory is created on disk**.

dsh-preset-gpt-6-astra README · Upgrade and maintenance (important)：After upgrading dsh, re-sync the baseline and rebuild:

```bash

dsh-preset-gpt-6-astra README · 1) replace base/ with the new shipped standard：cp "$DSH_INSTALL/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-presets/presets/standard/agent.cordis.yml" \
   base/standard.agent.cordis.yml
section: 1) replace base/ with the new shipped standard

text:
dsh-preset-gpt-6-astra README · 2) rebuild + self-check：node scripts/build.mjs
node scripts/check.mjs
dsh-preset-gpt-6-astra README · 3) install/update, then start one session in the GUI to confirm：dsh plugin --profile web update dsh-preset-gpt-6-astra     # method A
section: 3) install/update, then start one session in the GUI to confirm

text:
dsh-preset-gpt-6-astra README · or: bash scripts/install.sh / pwsh -File scripts/install.ps1 -Force：```

Step 2 is where an upstream `standard` rewrite surfaces: the `PATCHES` anchors are
checked, so a model, skill, or subagent row that upstream restructured fails the build
with the patch label instead of quietly reverting to upstream behaviour.

dsh-preset-gpt-6-astra README · Known limitations：- The Codex product surfaces the source mentions (Apps / Connectors, Plugins, Artifacts,
  `request_permissions`, `end_conversation`, the Guardian reviewer, the realtime backend)
  do not exist in dsh and are explicitly excluded by the adaptation section; for
  cross-session memory, use this machine's memory service (OpenViking) tools.
- The source is written against OpenAI's product surface. This preset uses it only as
  persona and behavioural guidance; it does not change model routing and does not
  represent any official position of OpenAI or DeepSeek — `{{model}}` states which model
  is actually answering.
- Any edit to the persona text changes the system-prompt prefix and therefore rebuilds
  the KV cache.
- A spawned subagent's persona is shorter than its parent's. Delete the `persona:` line
  from the spawn row in `preset/agent.cordis.yml` (and rebuild) to give children the full
  persona again.
